18-year-old Nethya shines with gold for Sri Lanka ‎

cards.what_happened: Eighteen-year-old Nethya Sampath cleared 2.08 metres to win Sri Lanka's first gold at the BIMSTEC Under-23 Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar, India. He did it in one attempt and had a personal best of 2.13 metres. Dineth Induwara Weeraratna also won gold in the men's 100 metres.
details: Nethya Sampath, an eighteen-year-old high jumper from Maris Stella College Thimbirigaskatuwa, won Sri Lanka's first gold. He did this at the BIMSTEC Under-23 Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar, India, which started on Wednesday.
Nethya cleared 2.08 metres in one attempt, and his personal best is 2.13 metres. India's Binoy and Ambriesh also cleared 2.08 metres but needed more than one attempt.

Dineth Induwara Weeraratna won the men's 100 metres in 10.35 seconds. India's Rushiprasad Desai was second, and Sri Lanka's Saad Jamaldeen was third. Sri Lanka also had a runner-up finish in the 1500 metres.
key_facts: Eighteen-year-old Nethya Sampath won Sri Lanka's first gold.
He cleared 2.08 metres in one attempt.
Dineth Induwara Weeraratna won men's 100m in 10.35 seconds.
India won six of the eight gold medals.
Sri Lanka won two golds in athletics.
cards.blurb: Teen Nethya Sampath cleared 2.08 metres to give Sri Lanka its first athletics gold.
cards.spoken: Sri Lanka have started their athletics campaign at the BIMSTEC Under-23 Championships in Bhubaneswar, India. The event began on Wednesday, and eighteen-year-old Nethya Sampath from Maris Stella College Thimbirigaskatuwa gave the team its first gold. He cleared two point oh eight metres in the high jump, and he did it in one attempt. His personal best is two point one three metres. A teammate, Dineth Induwara Weeraratna, also won gold in the men's hundred metres, finishing in ten point three five seconds. India did well on the first day, while Sri Lanka took two golds. The championships bring together more than two hundred athletes from six nations.

Easter attacks probe: New revelations in Suresh Sallay case

cards.what_happened: The Attorney General’s Department disclosed fresh findings against retired Major General Suresh Sallay over allegations of concealing information and misleading investigations into the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks. At Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court, Additional Solicitor General Dileepa Peiris said Sallay and Azad Maulana stayed at the same hotel in Ahungalla on August 15 and 16, 2020, and that Sallay changed his position when questioned about telephone records. The court also heard about a medical report, an alleged informant, and a possible former Deputy Inspector General of Police, and the case was set for January 27, 2027.
details: The Attorney General’s Department disclosed fresh findings in the investigation against former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, retired Major General Suresh Sallay, over allegations of concealing information and misleading investigations into the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks. At Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court, Additional Solicitor General Dileepa Peiris said investigations established that Sallay and Azad Maulana, who appeared in a Channel 4 documentary on the Easter attacks, stayed with their families at the same hotel in Ahungalla on August 15 and 16, 2020.

Peiris said Sallay first claimed the encounter was coincidental but later changed his position when questioned about telephone records. The Additional Solicitor General argued the circumstantial evidence lent credibility to certain claims made by Maulana. He also alleged that an informant known as Thambi Anna provided military intelligence with information regarding Zahran Hashim six months before the Easter Sunday attacks, and that the relevant file was concealed with Sallay’s knowledge.

Investigators are also looking into the possible involvement of a former Deputy Inspector General of Police. The court was told that a 31-page report by a five-member specialist medical panel, appointed to examine allegations of torture against Sallay while in detention, had been received. Peiris argued Sallay reported psychological stress but did not disclose physical torture to the medical panel.

Bhanuka Mallawarachchi, appearing for Sallay, disputed the prosecution’s interpretation and said the medical report referred to a degrading physical examination of his client. The defence also pointed out that the medical panel recommended further investigations into alleged mistreatment during detention. Peiris told the court that, in his opinion, sufficient evidence existed against former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa to name him as a suspect, but any decision to arrest him rested with investigating officers; after considering submissions from both parties, Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena ordered the case taken up again on January 27, 2027, for a report on the progress of investigations.
key_facts: Attorney General’s Department disclosed fresh findings against retired Major General Suresh Sallay.
Allegations concern concealing information and misleading investigations into 2019 Easter Sunday attacks.
Dileepa Peiris said Sallay and Azad Maulana stayed at Ahungalla hotel August 15 and 16, 2020.
Sallay first called encounter coincidental, then changed position over telephone records.
Prosecution alleged Thambi Anna gave military intelligence on Zahran Hashim six months before attacks.
File concealed with Sallay’s knowledge; former Deputy Inspector General of Police also examined.
31-page five-member specialist medical report received; defence cited degrading examination and further investigations.
Peiris said former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa could be suspect; arrest decision rests with investigators; case returns January 27, 2027.
cards.whats_next: The case will be taken up again on January 27, 2027, for a report on the progress of investigations.

Peiris also alleged an informant called Thambi Anna gave military intelligence about Zahran Hashim six months before the attacks, and a file was concealed with Sallay’s knowledge.
